segments.t: Outside the soundstage, veteran actor Guy Marchand catches up with his longtime agent Arlette Azémar. Accompanied by her dog Jean Gabin, Arlette offers warm encouragement before Guy returns to his shoot. Listen to the scene in French first.
Désolé pour mon agitation tout à l'heure.
Tu n'as pas à t'excuser, Guy.
Ton chien Jean Gabin est vraiment gentil.
Il a du flair, comme sa maîtresse.
C'est vrai, tu devines toujours les problèmes.
Je connais mes acteurs depuis longtemps.
Pourquoi tout le monde t'appelle Arlette Davidson?
Parce que je roule toujours en moto!
Tu es une femme libre et rebelle.
J'ai toujours refusé de faire des concessions.
Tu m'as souvent sauvé sur les tournages.
C'est le travail d'une bonne agente.
Merci d'être venue aujourd'hui, Arlette Davidson.
Je serai toujours là pour mes amis.
Maintenant, je peux retourner tourner sereinement.
Vas-y, Guy, montre-leur ton immense talent!
Let's examine how Arlette and Guy share a touching moment of friendship.
Désolé pour mon agitation tout à l'heure.
'Sorry for my agitation earlier.' Guy apologizes for his visible stress. A concise spoken phrase built around the French noun for 'agitation'.
Tu n'as pas à t'excuser, Guy.
'You do not have to apologize, Guy.' Arlette dismisses his concern gently. Listen for the expression meaning 'not', which leads naturally into 'to apologize'.
Ton chien Jean Gabin est vraiment gentil.
'Your dog Jean Gabin is really nice.' Guy compliments her companion. Guy opens with the word for 'dog' and lands on 'nice' at the close.
Il a du flair, comme sa maîtresse.
'He has a good nose, like his mistress.' Arlette makes a humorous comparison. The masculine noun flair refers to intuition or keen scent.
C'est vrai, tu devines toujours les problèmes.
'It is true, you always guess the problems.' Guy acknowledges her sharp intuition. Guy opens with the word for 'it is' and lands on 'problems' at the close.
Je connais mes acteurs depuis longtemps.
'I have known my actors for a long time.' Arlette explains her deep experience. Arlette pairs the verb meaning 'know' with the noun for 'actors'.
Pourquoi tout le monde t'appelle Arlette Davidson?
'Why does everyone call you Arlette Davidson?' Guy asks about her famous nickname. The compound name Arlette Davidson evokes the motorcycle brand.
Parce que je roule toujours en moto!
'Because I always ride a motorcycle!' Arlette proudly reveals the origin. The adverb meaning 'always' sharpens the verb for 'ride' here.
Tu es une femme libre et rebelle.
'You are a free and rebellious woman.' Guy praises her independent spirit. Guy opens with the word for 'are' and lands on 'rebellious' at the close.
J'ai toujours refusé de faire des concessions.
'I always refused to make concessions.' Arlette speaks of her lifelong principles. Listen for the expression meaning 'I have', which leads naturally into 'concession'.
Tu m'as souvent sauvé sur les tournages.
'You often saved me on movie shoots.' Guy expresses sincere gratitude. The key word here means 'have me', paired with 'shoots' to make the point clear.
C'est le travail d'une bonne agente.
'It is the job of a good agent.' Arlette defines her professional duty. Arlette pairs the verb meaning 'it is' with the noun for 'agent'.
Merci d'être venue aujourd'hui, Arlette Davidson.
'Thanks for coming today, Arlette Davidson.' Guy repeats her affectionate nickname. Notice how the verb for 'having' leads straight into 'thank you'.
Je serai toujours là pour mes amis.
'I will always be there for my friends.' Arlette reaffirms her enduring loyalty. Arlette opens with the word for 'will be' and lands on 'friends' at the close.
Maintenant, je peux retourner tourner sereinement.
'Now, I can return to filming peacefully.' Guy feels calm and focused again. The key word here means 'now', paired with 'peacefully' to make the point clear.
Vas-y, Guy, montre-leur ton immense talent!
